questions.q: Define verbal irony and situational irony in your own words, and give one example of each from "नवलेखन संस्मरण" without quoting the text directly.
questions.a: Verbal irony: a speaker says the opposite of what they mean (e.g., लाहको calling the child "अनपढ़" while the child teaches him humanity). Situational irony: outcome contradicts expectation (e.g., the "educated" लाहको behaves pettily while the "illiterate" child displays wisdom). A wrong answer that confuses the two or gives generic definitions (not from the text) reveals the student cannot distinguish irony types or locate them in the narrative.

questions.q: The threshold (चौखट) of the railway station appears repeatedly. Explain what it symbolizes and how its meaning shifts between the first and last time Naval crosses it.
questions.a: The threshold symbolizes the boundary between segregated social worlds (caste/class divisions) and the possibility of crossing into shared humanity. Initially, it represents exclusion — Naval hesitates, aware of his "place." By the end, after लाहको's transformation, it becomes a permeable membrane where connection occurs. A wrong answer that treats it only as a physical doorframe misses the symbolic evolution tied to character arc.

questions.q: In the scene where लाहको feeds Naval (खिलाना), identify the verbal irony in लाहको's dialogue and explain how the act of feeding functions as a symbol that subverts the power dynamic established earlier.
questions.a: Verbal irony: लाहको says "तुम्हें भूख लगी होगी" (you must be hungry) while he himself is emotionally starved for connection — he projects his need onto the child. Feeding symbolizes nurturing equality: earlier लाहको withheld food/affection to assert dominance; now offering it freely signifies surrender of ego. A wrong answer that only describes the plot action ("he gave food") without analyzing the irony-symbol interplay shows surface-level reading.

questions.q: Compare the irony in लाहको's transformation with the irony in उखु (Ukhu)'s role. How do both serve the theme but through different ironic structures?
questions.a: लाहको: dramatic irony — the reader sees his prejudice crumbling before he admits it; his "education" is ironically undone by a child's instinct. उखु: situational irony — the marginalized, "unclean" sweeper becomes the moral compass, guiding लाहको to humanity. Both invert social hierarchy: लाहको's irony is internal (self-deception), उखु's is external (society's misjudgment). A wrong answer that treats both as identical "role reversals" misses the structural difference (dramatic vs. situational) and thematic nuance.

questions.q: Evaluate this claim: "The lamp (दीपक) at the station is the central symbol of the story because it represents knowledge." Defend or refute using at least two textual moments.
questions.a: Refute. The lamp appears briefly as a physical light source; it does not accumulate meaning across scenes. The true central symbol is the act of *crossing the threshold* (चौखट पार करना), which recurs structurally: Naval entering the station, लाहको stepping out of his prejudice, उखु bridging worlds. The lamp is a prop; the threshold is a motif. A wrong answer that accepts the claim reveals inability to distinguish fleeting image from sustained structural symbol.

questions.q: Write a 4-line paragraph continuing the story: Naval returns to the station ten years later. Use one irony and one symbol from the original text, but invert their original meaning.
questions.a: Example: "The threshold Naval once crossed trembling now bears his name — ironic, since the stationmaster who once barred him now salutes. The lamp he once watched from afar now burns in his hand, not as borrowed light but as his own earned wisdom." A poor answer that merely repeats original symbols without inversion (e.g., "he crosses the threshold again") shows inability to creatively manipulate literary devices.
